title: Unstable props of grace-universality: Word-offers confused with a decretive will to save all
pass_a_gloss: But the Hypotheses on which this Universality of Grace rests, although the reason & scope of the Lutherans is diverse from that of the Remonstrants, have been indicated in part above, at the Articles controversed with the Arminians I. II. III. IV. &c. And they are understood from what follows as well. Specifically, however, there are confused God's commands, & the promises in the Word, which are to be proposed indiscriminately by the Ministers of the Gospel, with the will or good-pleasure in God of saving all & each: Thus is confused the universality of believers, of those to be saved, & the universality of human beings; all human beings taken collectively, thence from Adam, & any human beings distributively, as elsewhere at length. So vocation through nature, by which God is manifested, and His common goodness; or vocation made sometimes in the greater ones; or that former vocation of the Hebrews, celebrated among some but few & neighboring Nations; or that which was to be done by the Apostles every way, generally & promiscuously, &c. Matthew 18; Mark 16. These (I say) vocations are precariously dragged to a universal Vocation of all & each human beings, & to a sufficient offering of the means of salvation, &c. But of that common & universal Vocation even before Christ was exhibited, at length above, Controv. with the Remonstrants XXXI.
pass_b_english: But the hypotheses on which this universality of grace rests — though the Lutherans' reason and aim differ from the Remonstrants' — have already been pointed out in part above, under the articles controversed with the Arminians, I, II, III, IV, and so on. They are also clear from what follows.

In particular, God's commands and the promises in the Word, which gospel ministers are to set out indiscriminately, are confused with a will or good-pleasure in God to save all and each. So the universality of believers — of those who are to be saved — is confused with the universality of human beings: all humans taken collectively from Adam onward, and any humans taken distributively, as is shown at length elsewhere.

Likewise vocation through nature, by which God is manifested, and His common goodness; or vocation given at times in the greater ones; or that former Hebrew vocation, well known among some few neighboring nations; or the vocation the Apostles were to carry out every way, generally and promiscuously, and so on (Matthew 18; Mark 16). These vocations, I say, are precariously dragged into a universal vocation of all human beings and each one, and into a sufficient offering of the means of salvation, and so on.
But of that common and universal vocation even before Christ was exhibited, see at length above, Controv. with the Remonstrants XXXI.
source_text: Hypotheses verò quibus haec Universalitas Gratiae nititur, quamvis diversa sit ratio & scopus Lutheranorum à Remonstrantium illo, suprâ sunt ex parte indicatae, ad Articulos cum Arminianis controversos I. II. III. IV. &c. Et ex sequentibus quoque intelliguntur. In specie verò confunduntur, Dei mandata, & promissiones in Verbo, à Ministris Euangelii indiscriminatim proponendae; cum voluntate seu beneplacito in Deo omnes & singulos salvandi: Sic confusa universalitas credentium, servandorum, & universalitas hominum; omnes homines collectivè sumpti, indè ab Adamo, & quivis homines distributivè ut prolixè aliàs. Ità vocatio per naturam, quâ Deus manifestatur, ejusque communis bonitas; aut vocatio facta quandoque in majoribus; aut Hebraeorum illa quondam, celebris inter nonnullas sed paucas & viciniores Gentes; aut quae facienda per Apostolos quaquaversum fuit, generatim & promiscuè, &c. Matth. xviii. Marc. xvi. Istae (inquam) vocationes precariè trahuntur ad Vocationem universalem, omnium & singulorum hominum, & ad sufficientem oblationem mediorum salutis, &c. Sed de Vocatione illa communi, & universali etiam antè Christum exhibitum, prolixè suprâ, Controv. cum Remonstr. XXXI.
